Let \(m\) be the number of edges used, and let \(r=12-m\) be unused edges.

In any trail, at most two vertices can have odd degree in the used-edge graph. The cube has all 8 vertices of degree \(3\). If a vertex has \(u\) unused incident edges, then its used degree is \(3-u\), which is odd exactly when \(u\) is even. Thus at most two vertices can have an even number of unused incident edges.

If \(r\le 2\), then the total number of unused-edge incidences is \(2r\le 4\). But with at most two even-\(u\) vertices, the other at least six vertices must have odd \(u\ge 1\), requiring at least \(6\) incidences—impossible. Therefore \(r\ge 3\), so \(m\le 9\).

This is achievable: remove three disjoint cube edges, leaving a graph with exactly two odd vertices, so it has an Euler trail of 9 edges starting at \(A\).

Thus the greatest distance is
\[
9 \times 12 = 108.
\]

\[
\boxed{108}
\]
